architecture.description: Dual encoder CLIP-style: ResNet-50 visual encoder (ImageNet-initialised) + BioClinicalBERT text encoder; clip embedding = average of per-frame embeddings
architecture.params: not stated (ResNet-50 ~25M + BioClinicalBERT ~110M standard figures; each weight zip ~495 MB)
architecture.input: frames (or clips as sets of frames, average-pooled); preprocessing resize 360x640 then centre crop 224

quotes.quote: We employ the ResNet-50 model (He et al., 2016) pretrained on ImageNet as the base architecture for the visual encoder F .
For a given video clip v, we first sample a fixed number of frames {z0 , ..., zT } and then feed them through F
We utilize the dual-encoder architecture with ResNet50 [21] as visual encoder and ClinicalBert [22] as textual encoder, respectively.
transforms.Resize((360, 640)), transforms.CenterCrop(224),
text_bert_type='emilyalsentzer/Bio_ClinicalBERT'

pretraining_data.summary: SVL: 1,326 surgical video lectures (~300 h) crawled from WebSurg (1,124 via keywords) and EAES + YouTube (202), with ASR narration; HecVL/PeskaVLP reuse SVL with metadata-derived hierarchical / LLM-augmented texts
pretraining_data.youtube_derived: YES - partly (EAES and YouTube lectures); WebSurg lectures are web-crawled from the IRCAD e-learning platform

quotes.quote: we query the videos based on keywords from three online platforms, i.e., Websurg (Websurg, 2023), EAES (EAES, 2023), and YouTube (YouTube, 2023).
For Websurg, we use “intervention” and “laparoscopic” as keywords to crawl 1, 124 surgical lectures.
For EAES and YouTube, we manually collect 202 surgical video lectures using manually designed keywords.

Pretraining dataset: we use the surgical lecture videos from the Surgical Video Lecture dataset (SVL) for the pretraining, which was proposed by the SurgVLP [22].
In this work, we use this hierarchical video-language pretraining dataset and perform hierarchical knowledge augmentation to improve the textual quality.

appendix300_in_pretraining.reason: Pretraining videos are keyword-crawled lectures from WebSurg/EAES/YouTube; individual videos and their originating hospitals are not listed, so inclusion of a Dresden-area appendectomy recording cannot be excluded (WebSurg 'General and digestive surgery' lectures are in scope).

quotes.quote: They cover the five main categories, “Hepatobiliary and pancreatic surgery”, “General and digestive surgery”, “Bariatric surgery”, “Hernia surgery” and “Colorectal, transanal and proctological surgery”.

eligibility.notes: Documented at the level of sources/platforms and counts (not a per-video list). Visual encoder is a frame-level ResNet-50.
